id: La Voz del Pueblo (Colombian press history notes)
title: La Voz del Pueblo (Colombian press history notes)
text: From a short survey of nineteenth-century Colombian newspapers: La Voz del Pueblo, whose name means People's Voice, was a small liberal paper printed in Bogotá. According to these notes it was launched in 1852 and appeared once a week, every Sunday. Its editors opposed the government of the day, and the paper lasted only a few months, ending after its ninth number.

title: ICON convention (fan wiki)
text: ICON is the long-running sci-fi and fantasy fan gathering of eastern Iowa, held each autumn around Cedar Rapids and Iowa City. Fan wiki entry: the very first ICON took place in 1979, organised by student fans who had grown out of a university science fiction club started by Joe Haldeman. Today the Mindbridge Foundation runs it alongside AnimeIowa and Gamicon, and fans call it the state's oldest and biggest convention of its kind.

title: Avant-Pop anthology (bookseller catalogue entry)
text: Catalogue entry, small-press fiction shelf: Avant-Pop: Fiction for a Daydream Nation, edited by the critic Larry McCaffery, first edition 1994, Black Ice Books imprint of Fiction Collective Two. An anthology mixing experimental stories, comics and hard-to-classify texts. Contributors include Kathy Acker, Samuel R. Delany, Mark Leyner and William T. Vollmann. Good condition, light wear to the cover.

title: Genesis Suite (concert programme note)
text: Programme note for tonight's performance. The Genesis Suite dates from 1947. Conductor Nathaniel Shilkret had the idea of setting the opening chapters of the Book of Genesis for speaker, choir and orchestra, and he commissioned seven composers to write one movement each, writing one himself. Schoenberg supplied the opening prelude and Stravinsky the closing Babel movement, while several of the others were Hollywood film composers.

id: Tom King and the Starfires (Cleveland music newsletter)
title: Tom King and the Starfires (Cleveland music newsletter)
text: From our local music newsletter's look back at Cleveland rock history: guitarist Tom King put together his first group, the Starfires, in 1961 while still a teenager. The Starfires later turned into the Outsiders, a new name that Capitol Records insisted on before releasing their hit Time Won't Let Me. Not to be confused with the Los Angeles garage band that used the same name in the 1960s.

title: The Horror Zine (genre magazine directory)
text: Directory listing: The Horror Zine. Genre: horror and dark fantasy fiction, poetry and art. Based in Sacramento, California. Founded in 2006 by editor Jeani Rector, with Dean H. Wild as assistant editor. Notable contributors over the years include Ramsey Campbell, Joe R. Lansdale, Graham Masterton and Bentley Little. Submissions are accepted from new and established authors.

title: TRANSFER Gallery (Brooklyn arts listings)
text: Brooklyn arts listings: TRANSFER is an exhibition space for internet-based artists, opened in 2015 by curator Kelani Nichole, who still directs it. The idea behind the space is to take work that normally lives on screens and let artists rebuild it inside an empty white room, using paint, drawing, sculpture or photographs. The name refers to that move from online to physical.

title: 7Horse (soundtrack fan site)
text: Soundtrack fan site profile: 7Horse is a two-piece blues-rock act made up of Phil Leavitt on drums and lead vocals and Joie Calio on guitar and bass, both also known from the band dada. The pair started playing as 7Horse in 2008. They are best known for Meth Lab Zoso Sticker, the song heard in the trailer and on the soundtrack of The Wolf of Wall Street.

title: Jared Rushton (child actors fan page)
text: Fan page for child stars of the 1980s: Jared Rushton was born on March 3, 1972. He appeared in Big, Overboard and Honey, I Shrunk the Kids, later had a part in Pet Sematary Two and played Chip on the sitcom Roseanne. He earned Saturn Award and Young Artist Award nominations before leaving acting for music; he now plays guitar with the rock group Deal by Dusk.

title: Traceroute (film festival catalogue)
text: Festival catalogue: Traceroute, a 2014 documentary by Austrian artist and director Johannes Grenzfurthner. Part road movie, part personal essay, the film travels across the United States to explore where nerd culture came from and where it is heading. Produced together with the art collective monochrom and Reisenbauer Film, with a soundtrack featuring Kasson Crooker and Hans Nieswandt.
